description: Play Endless Craft free: mix water, fire, earth and air, then let an AI invent every combination beyond the classic book. Discoveries never end.
lede: Endless Craft is a free element mixing game on a magic workbench. You begin with water, fire, earth and air. Mix any two and see what happens: the classics come from a hand-written book of 692 elements, and everything beyond it is invented on the spot by an AI — so there is always one more discovery waiting.

p: You start with four elements: water, fire, earth and air. Place two of them together on the table and they become something new — water and fire make steam, earth and water make mud, and steam on mud makes clay. Every discovery joins your list on the side, ready to be mixed again.

Behind the scenes there are two layers. The classic book holds 692 hand-written elements and 1,345 recipes, and those pairs resolve instantly, even offline, exactly as written. Any other pair is sent to an AI, which invents a result and an emoji for it — a lava lamp, moon cheese, a time machine, things nobody wrote down. The answer is saved on your device, so the same pair always gives you the same element, and your inventions can be mixed further, again and again.

If the AI cannot be reached, the mix is not lost: it fizzles into a humble by-product such as sludge or goo, and you can try the pair again later. There is no total to complete and no win screen — the counter simply counts everything you have discovered, and the fun is in seeing how strange your collection gets.
Every element grows from the four you start with. These ten are made straight from them, all from the classic book, so they work instantly. Everything after that is up to you — and the AI.

ol: Mix every new element with water, fire, earth and air first. Between them, the four basics appear in 154 of the classic recipes, and fire and water are two of the busiest elements in the whole book.
Try an element with a copy of itself. Two of the same often make something bigger: two bricks make a wall, two walls a house and two houses a village.
Think about what happens in real life. Heat changes things, cold freezes them, water washes and wind wears things down. Time is an element too, and it makes plants grow into trees.
Once the book runs out, keep mixing anyway — that is where the AI takes over, and the stranger the pair, the better the invention.
Your inventions are real elements: mix them with anything, including each other, and the chain never has to end.
A fizzle is not a failure: it means the AI was out of reach just then. The same pair may invent something when you try it again later.
A gold star marks a classic final element — one the book neither makes nor uses. AI elements never get the star: they can always be mixed further.
Use the search box when your list gets long. Typing just a few letters is enough.

p: Your discoveries — including everything the AI invents for you — and every pair result are saved in this browser on this device, along with whatever is sitting on your table, so you can close the tab and carry on later. Starting over from the reset button forgets everything, inventions included, and hands you back the four basics.

sections.h: Where the four elements come from
p: The notion that everything is built from a few simple elements is about 2,500 years old: the Greek philosopher Empedocles proposed earth, water, air and fire as the four roots of all things. Mixing games turned that idea into a puzzle in the 2010s, and AI crafting games made it endless — there is always one more combination nobody has tried. Endless Craft keeps both halves: a hand-written book for the classics, and an AI for everything after.

Looking for another relaxed puzzle? Grow a giant watermelon in [[fruit-merge]], or find the pairs in [[memory-match]]. For a quick break between discoveries, see how round you can draw in [[perfect-circle]] or test your reflexes in the [[reaction-time-test]]. You will find more games like this among the [[cat:puzzle|puzzle games]] and [[cat:casual|casual games]].

faq: Is Endless Craft free to play?
Yes. It is completely free, with no account, no download and nothing to unlock. It runs in your browser on a phone, tablet or computer.

There is no fixed number — that is the point. The classic book inside the game has 692 elements, and beyond those the AI invents new ones for pairs nobody wrote a recipe for, so the total grows with everything you try.
How does the AI part work?

When you mix a pair the classic book does not know, the two element names are sent to an AI, which replies with a new element and an emoji. The answer is saved on your device, so that pair is instant — and identical — forever after.
Will the same pair always give the same result?

For you, yes. Classic pairs come from the fixed book, and AI answers are stored on your device the first time you get them. Another player might receive a different invention for the same pair — every collection is personal.
What happens if the AI is unavailable?
The mix fizzles into a by-product like sludge, goo or vapor instead of failing, and the classic book keeps working offline. Try the pair again later and the AI may invent something for it then.
Is Endless Craft the same as Alchemy Lab?

Endless Craft grew out of Alchemy Lab and keeps its entire classic book — the same 692 elements and 1,345 recipes — then removes the ceiling: instead of ending when the book runs out, it hands unknown pairs to the AI and lets you discover forever.
Does the order of the two elements matter?
No. Water with fire and fire with water both make steam. Every pair works in either order.
Can I mix an element with itself?
Yes. Tap it twice in your list, or double tap it on the table to make a copy and then put the two together.
Does my progress carry across devices?
No. Discoveries and AI inventions live in the browser on the device you play on, which is also why no account is needed. A different phone or browser starts its own collection.
